objective: A player in the channel can ask the bot how to get the app, how to update it, and whether the copy they already have is current — without an operator and without a GitHub account. Today the only slash command is /suggest, and the only public download is Release v0.1.0 from 2026-07-26, whose Windows zip was packaged at 7465386 — a commit whose scripts/package_mvp_windows.ps1 contains the string 'overlay' zero times. Overlay bundling landed at c824050 on 2026-08-04, nine days later. The announcement standing in the channel right now says the overlay is in the download and starts with run.bat; a command pointing at releases/latest today hands the player a zip with no overlay in it and industrialises that contradiction. So this stage is gated on TASK-304-S1 (issue 177, orchestrator-owned, .github/** is PROTECTED) publishing a release built at or after c824050. Beyond the how-to, the command answers the question a returning player actually has — 'am I on the current build?' — by reading the most recently announced range_end and posted_at from the release_announce table the bot already owns, so the answer needs no GitHub API call in the command path.
constraints: PRECONDITION, CHECKED FIRST AND AT ZERO TOKEN COST: `gh release view --json assets -q '.assets[].name'` must show a `*-windows-x64.zip` whose build id S satisfies `git merge-base --is-ancestor c824050 S`. If it does not, STOP and report needs_retry with that check's output. Do NOT soften the copy to match a stale release, do NOT link the Actions-artifact route (it 401s without a logged-in GitHub account and the artifacts expire), and do NOT ship an 'ask an operator' answer. Waiting for S1 is the correct outcome here; shipping a truthful-sounding link to a zip with no overlay in it is not.

Register /download on bot.tree next to /suggest, as a second app_commands.command in bot/bot.py. It replies ephemerally (only the asker sees it) and is NOT gated to SUGGEST_CHANNEL_ID — a player asking where the download is should get an answer wherever they ask.

Copy must match packaging/README.txt fact for fact. Where the two disagree the player hits the disagreement on their first run, and packaging/README.txt is out of scope here, so the command bends to it: Windows x86-64 only (the Linux tarball is dev/CI, macOS is dropped), Python 3.10+, run.bat is THE entrypoint, the overlay starts automatically with run.bat, Ctrl+Alt+D, OVERLAY_HOTKEY overrides it, run.bat --no-overlay runs the web page alone, and first launch takes tens of seconds because of a one-time dependency and data-cache step.

The 'am I current?' answer must be mechanical, not a vibe: the zip filename carries its build id (poe-upgrade-advisor-v0-<build>-windows-x64.zip), and the player compares the one they downloaded against the newest asset on the releases page.

Read the announced build from the EXISTING bot.db handle inside the command callback — `SELECT range_end, posted_at FROM release_announce WHERE posted_at IS NOT NULL ORDER BY rowid DESC LIMIT 1`. No new sqlite connection, no GitHub API call, no network in the command path. Report the short id (first 7 chars) and posted_at.

An empty or posted_at-NULL release_announce is the normal state of a fresh database, not an error: say plainly that no build has been announced yet and give the releases URL. No fabricated version, no traceback, no silent empty field.

The reply goes through scrub and carries no task id, packet path, ledger id or role name, and stays under Discord's 2000-character message limit — assert the limit in a test rather than eyeballing it.
Do not touch /suggest, the S3 announce loop or its green gate, relay_decisions, publish_weekly_digests, on_message, open_database's schema/migration, bot/release_notes.py or bot/digest.py.
Existing tests in tests/test_bot.py may be EXTENDED; no existing test is deleted, skipped or weakened. tests/test_announce.py, tests/test_digest.py and bot/tests/ stay byte-identical to main.
Branch backend/TASK-304-S2-<slug>. A literal role/... branch is refused by completion proof #4.

Issue 178 is a STAGE issue and closing it is correct: write 'Fixes #178' exactly once in the PR body. Never write a bare '#97' in any commit message or PR body — the ORG mission issue must stay open; refer to it as 'issue 97'. Check before pushing: `gh pr view <n> --json body -q .body | grep -c '#97'` must be 0.
forbidden_actions: Shipping the command against a release whose Windows zip predates c824050
Linking the Actions-artifact download route, or telling a player to ask an operator
Calling the GitHub API, or opening a second sqlite connection, from the command callback
Fabricating a version when release_announce has no posted row
Contradicting packaging/README.txt on platform, entrypoint, hotkey or --no-overlay
Modifying /suggest, the announce loop or its green gate, relay_decisions, publish_weekly_digests, on_message, or anything under .github/
required_checks: python3 -m pytest tests/test_bot.py tests/test_announce.py tests/test_digest.py bot/tests/test_release_notes.py -q

acceptance_criteria.text: Before any other work, the latest GitHub Release carries a *-windows-x64.zip whose build id S satisfies `git merge-base --is-ancestor c824050 S`; if it does not, the stage stops and reports needs_retry with the check output, having modified nothing.

/download is registered on bot.tree alongside /suggest, replies ephemerally, and is not gated to SUGGEST_CHANNEL_ID; a test invokes its callback with a channel id other than SUGGEST_CHANNEL_ID and asserts a real answer is returned ephemerally.

The reply states the releases URL, Windows x86-64 only, Python 3.10+, run.bat as THE entrypoint that starts the overlay automatically, Ctrl+Alt+D, OVERLAY_HOTKEY as the override, and run.bat --no-overlay for the web page alone; a test asserts each of those seven facts appears in the sent text.

The reply explains updating: download the newest zip, extract to a NEW folder, run run.bat there, and expect the one-time dependency/cache step again on first launch; a test asserts the new-folder instruction and the first-launch note are present, and no statement contradicts packaging/README.txt.

The reply tells the player how to check whether their copy is current by the build id in the zip filename (poe-upgrade-advisor-v0-<build>-windows-x64.zip) compared against the newest asset on the releases page; a test asserts the filename pattern appears.

The reply reports the most recently announced build as one line carrying the 7-character range_end and its posted_at, read from the existing bot.db handle with a single SELECT and no network call; a test seeds release_announce with a posted row and asserts both values appear, and asserts the callback makes no GitHub API call.

With release_announce empty (or every row posted_at NULL) the reply says no build has been announced yet and still gives the releases URL; a test covers both cases and asserts no exception and no fabricated version string.
The reply passes scrub, contains no task id, packet path, ledger id or role name, and is at most 2000 characters; a test asserts the length bound and the absence of internal tokens.
bot/README.md documents /download, its single release_announce read, and that it is not channel-gated.

Both required checks pass; no existing test is deleted, skipped or weakened; /suggest, the announce loop and its green gate, relay_decisions, publish_weekly_digests, on_message and open_database are unmodified, and bot/release_notes.py, bot/digest.py, tests/test_announce.py and tests/test_digest.py are byte-identical to main.

rollback: Revert the branch. The command is additive and reads one row; nothing it does is durable, so a revert is complete. If it has already answered a player with a wrong build id, the fix is forward — the reply is ephemeral and no correction post is owed.
